subparagraph.content: Maintenance, repair, and replacement activities for Indian dams under this section shall be carried out in accordance with the dam safety policies of the Director of the Bureau of Indian Affairs established to carry out the Indian Dams Safety Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 3801 et seq.).

subparagraph.heading: High hazard potential dams.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The dams eligible for funding under paragraph (1)(B)(i) are Indian high hazard potential dams in the United States that—

clause.content: are included in the safety of dams program established pursuant to the Indian Dams Safety Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 3801 et seq.); and

item.content: are owned by the Federal Government, as listed in the Federal inventory required by Executive Order 13327 (40 U.S.C. 121 note; relating to Federal real property asset management); and
are managed by the Bureau of Indian Affairs (including dams managed under contracts or compacts pursuant to the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5301 et seq.)); or

subclause.content: have deferred maintenance documented by the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

subparagraph.heading: Low hazard potential dams.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The dams eligible for funding under paragraph (1)(B)(ii) are Indian low hazard potential dams in the United States that, on the date of enactment of this Act—

clause.content: are covered under the Indian Dams Safety Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 3801 et seq.); and

item.content: are owned by the Federal Government, as listed in the Federal inventory required by Executive Order 13327 (40 U.S.C. 121 note; relating to Federal real property asset management); and
are managed by the Bureau of Indian Affairs (including dams managed under contracts or compacts pursuant to the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5301 et seq.)); or

subclause.content: have deferred maintenance documented by the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

paragraph.heading: Requirements and conditions.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act and as a precondition to amounts being expended from the Fund to carry out this subsection, the Secretary, in consultation with representatives of affected Indian tribes, shall develop and submit to Congress—

subparagraph.chapeau: programmatic goals to carry out this subsection that—

clause.content: would enable the completion of repairing, replacing, improving, or performing maintenance on Indian dams as expeditiously as practicable, subject to the dam safety policies of the Director of the Bureau of Indian Affairs established to carry out the Indian Dams Safety Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 3801 et seq.);
facilitate or improve the ability of the Bureau of Indian Affairs to carry out the mission of the Bureau of Indian Affairs in operating an Indian dam; and
ensure that the results of government-to-government consultation required under paragraph (4) be addressed; and

subparagraph.chapeau: funding prioritization criteria to serve as a methodology for distributing funds under this subsection that take into account—

clause.chapeau: the extent to which deferred maintenance of Indian dams poses a threat to—

subclause.content: public or employee safety or health;
natural or cultural resources; or
the ability of the Bureau of Indian Affairs to carry out the mission of the Bureau of Indian Affairs in operating an Indian dam;

clause.chapeau: the extent to which repairing, replacing, improving, or performing maintenance on an Indian dam will—

subclause.content: improve public or employee safety, health, or accessibility;
assist in compliance with codes, standards, laws, or other requirements;
address unmet needs; or
assist in protecting natural or cultural resources;

clause.content: the methodology of the rehabilitation priority index of the Secretary, as in effect on the date of enactment of this Act;
the potential economic benefits of the expenditures on job creation and general economic development in the affected tribal communities;
the ability of an Indian dam to address tribal, regional, and watershed level flood prevention needs;
the need to comply with the dam safety policies of the Director of the Bureau of Indian Affairs established to carry out the Indian Dams Safety Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 3801 et seq.);
the ability of the water storage capacity of an Indian dam to be increased to prevent flooding in downstream tribal and nontribal communities; and

such other factors as the Secretary determines to be appropriate to prioritize the use of available funds that are, to the fullest extent practicable, consistent with tribal and user recommendations received pursuant to the consultation and input process under paragraph (4).

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Except as provided in subparagraph (B), before expending funds on an Indian dam pursuant to paragraph (1) and not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall—

clause.content: consult with the Director of the Bureau of Indian Affairs on the expenditure of funds;

ensure that the Director of the Bureau of Indian Affairs advises the Indian tribe that has jurisdiction over the land on which a dam eligible to receive funding under paragraph (2) is located on the expenditure of funds; and
solicit and consider the input, comments, and recommendations of the landowners served by the Indian dam.

subparagraph.heading: Emergencies.—
subparagraph.content: If the Secretary determines that an emergency circumstance exists with respect to an Indian dam, subparagraph (A) shall not apply with respect to that Indian dam.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to subparagraph (B), to the maximum extent practicable, the Secretary shall ensure that, for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2030, each Indian dam eligible for funding under paragraph (2) that has critical maintenance needs receives part of the funding under paragraph (1) to address critical maintenance needs.

subparagraph.heading: Priority.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In allocating amounts under paragraph (1)(B), in addition to considering the funding priorities described in paragraph (3), the Secretary shall give priority to Indian dams eligible for funding under paragraph (2) that serve—

clause.content: more than 1 Indian tribe within an Indian reservation; or
highly populated Indian communities, as determined by the Secretary.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Subject to clause (ii), in allocating amounts under paragraph (1)(B), the Secretary shall allocate not more than $10,000,000 to any individual dam described in paragraph (2) during any consecutive 3-year period.

clause.heading: Exception.—
clause.content: Notwithstanding the cap described in clause (i), if the full amount under paragraph (1)(B) cannot be fully allocated to eligible Indian dams because the costs of the remaining activities authorized in paragraph (1)(B) of an Indian dam would exceed the cap described in clause (i), the Secretary may allocate the remaining funds to eligible Indian dams in accordance with this subsection.

subparagraph.heading: Basis of Funding.—
subparagraph.content: Any amounts made available under this paragraph shall be nonreimbursable.

subparagraph.heading: Applicability of ISDEAA.—
subparagraph.content: The Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5301 et seq.) shall apply to activities carried out under this paragraph.

subparagraph.heading: Establishment.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary of the Interior shall establish within the Bureau of Indian Affairs the Tribal Safety of Dams Committee (referred to in this paragraph as the “Committee”).

clause.heading: Composition.—
clause.chapeau: The Committee shall be composed of 15 members, of whom—

subclause.chapeau: 11 shall be appointed by the Secretary of the Interior from among individuals who, to the maximum extent practicable, have knowledge and expertise in dam safety issues and flood prevention and mitigation, of whom not less than 1 shall be a member of an Indian tribe in each of the Bureau of Indian Affairs regions of—

subclause.content: 2 shall be appointed by the Secretary of the Interior from among employees of the Bureau of Indian Affairs who have knowledge and expertise in dam safety issues and flood prevention and mitigation;
1 shall be appointed by the Secretary of the Interior from among employees of the Bureau of Reclamation who have knowledge and expertise in dam safety issues and flood prevention and mitigation; and
1 shall be appointed by the Secretary of the Army from among employees of the Corps of Engineers who have knowledge and expertise in dam safety issues and flood prevention and mitigation.

clause.heading: Nonvoting members.—
clause.content: The members of the Committee appointed under subclauses (II) and (III) of clause (i) shall be nonvoting members.

clause.heading: Date.—
clause.content: The appointments of the members of the Committee shall be made as soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act.

subparagraph.heading: Period of appointment.—
subparagraph.content: Members shall be appointed for the life of the Committee.

subparagraph.heading: Vacancies.—
subparagraph.content: Any vacancy in the Committee shall not affect the powers of the Committee, but shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment.

subparagraph.heading: Initial meeting.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 30 days after the date on which all members of the Committee have been appointed, the Committee shall hold the first meeting.

subparagraph.heading: Meetings.—
subparagraph.content: The Committee shall meet at the call of the Chairperson.

subparagraph.heading: Quorum.—
subparagraph.content: A majority of the members of the Committee shall constitute a quorum, but a lesser number of members may hold hearings.

subparagraph.heading: Chairperson and vice chairperson.—
subparagraph.content: The Committee shall select a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson from among the members.

subparagraph.heading: Study.—
subparagraph.content: The Committee shall conduct a thorough study of all matters relating to the modernization of the Indian Dams Safety Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 3801 et seq.).

subparagraph.heading: Recommendations.—
subparagraph.content: The Committee shall develop recommendations for legislation to improve the Indian Dams Safety Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 3801 et seq.).

subparagraph.heading: Report.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after the date on which the Committee holds the first meeting, the Committee shall submit a report containing a detailed statement of the findings and conclusions of the Committee, together with recommendations for legislation that the Committee considers appropriate, to—

clause.content: the Committee on Indian Affairs of the Senate; and
the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives.

subparagraph.heading: Hearings.—
subparagraph.content: The Committee may hold such hearings, sit and act at such times and places, take such testimony, and receive such evidence as the Committee considers appropriate to carry out this paragraph.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The Committee may secure directly from any Federal department or agency such information as the Committee considers necessary to carry out this paragraph.

clause.heading: Request.—
clause.content: On request of the Chairperson of the Committee, the head of any Federal department or agency shall furnish information described in clause (i) to the Committee.

subparagraph.heading: Postal services.—
subparagraph.content: The Committee may use the United States mails in the same manner and under the same conditions as other departments and agencies of the Federal Government.

subparagraph.heading: Gifts.—
subparagraph.content: The Committee may accept, use, and dispose of gifts or donations of services or property.

clause.heading: Non-federal members.—
clause.content: Each member of the Committee who is not an officer or employee of the Federal Government shall be compensated at a rate equal to the daily equivalent of the annual rate of basic pay prescribed for level IV of the Executive Schedule under section 5315 of title 5, United States Code, for each day (including travel time) during which the member is engaged in the performance of the duties of the Committee.

clause.heading: Federal members.—
clause.content: Each member of the Committee who is an officer or employee of the Federal Government shall serve without compensation in addition to that received for services as an officer or employee of the Federal Government.

subparagraph.heading: Travel expenses.—
subparagraph.content: The members of the Committee shall be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, at rates authorized for employees of agencies under subchapter I of chapter 57 of title 5, United States Code, while away from their homes or regular places of business in the performance of services for the Committee.

subclause.heading: Appointment.—
subclause.content: The Chairperson of the Committee may, without regard to the civil service laws and regulations, appoint and terminate an executive director and such other additional personnel as may be necessary to enable the Committee to perform the duties of the Committee.

subclause.heading: Confirmation.—
subclause.content: The employment of an executive director shall be subject to confirmation by the Committee.

clause.heading: Compensation.—
clause.content: The Chairperson of the Committee may fix the compensation of the executive director and other personnel without regard to chapter 51 and subchapter III of chapter 53 of title 5, United States Code, relating to classification of positions and General Schedule pay rates, except that the rate of pay for the executive director and other personnel may not exceed the rate payable for level V of the Executive Schedule under section 5316 of that title.

subparagraph.heading: Detail of government employees.—
subparagraph.content: Any Federal Government employee may be detailed to the Committee without reimbursement, and such detail shall be without interruption or loss of civil service status or privilege.

subparagraph.heading: Procurement of temporary and intermittent services.—
subparagraph.content: The Chairperson of the Committee may procure temporary and intermittent services under section 3109(b) of title 5, United States Code, at rates for individuals that do not exceed the daily equivalent of the annual rate of basic pay prescribed for level V of the Executive Schedule under section 5316 of that title.

paragraph.heading: Termination of the committee.—
paragraph.content: The Committee shall terminate 90 days after the date on which the Committee submits the report under paragraph (2)(C).

paragraph.heading: Funding.—
paragraph.content: Of the amounts authorized to be expended from either Fund, $1,000,000 shall be made available from either Fund during fiscal year 2017 to carry out this subsection, to remain available until expended.

paragraph.heading: Tribal reports.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall request that, not less frequently than once every 180 days, each Indian tribe submit to the Secretary a report providing an inventory of the dams located on the land of the Indian tribe.

paragraph.heading: BIA reports.—
paragraph.content: Not less frequently than once each year, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report describing the condition of each dam under the partial or total jurisdiction of the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish, within the Bureau of Indian Affairs, a flood plain management pilot program (referred to in this subsection as the “program”) to provide, at the request of an Indian tribe, guidance to the Indian tribe relating to best practices for the mitigation and prevention of floods, including consultation with the Indian tribe on—

subparagraph.content: flood plain mapping; or
new construction planning.

paragraph.heading: Termination.—
paragraph.content: The program shall terminate on the date that is 11 years after the date of enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Funding.—
paragraph.content: Of the amounts authorized to be expended from either Fund, $250,000 shall be made available from either Fund during each of fiscal years 2017 through 2026 to carry out this subsection, to remain available until expended.

subtitle.heading: Irrigation Rehabilitation and Renovation for Indian Tribal Governments and Their Economies

section.heading: DEFINITIONS.
section.chapeau: In this subtitle:

paragraph.heading: Deferred maintenance.—
paragraph.content: The term “deferred maintenance” means any maintenance activity that was delayed to a future date, in lieu of being carried out at the time at which the activity was scheduled to be, or otherwise should have been, carried out.

paragraph.heading: Fund.—
paragraph.content: The term “Fund” means the Indian Irrigation Fund established by section 3211.

paragraph.heading: Indian tribe.—
paragraph.content: The term “Indian tribe” has the meaning given the term in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5304).

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

section.heading: ESTABLISHMENT.
section.chapeau: There is established in the Treasury of the United States a fund, to be known as the “Indian Irrigation Fund”, consisting of—

paragraph.content: such amounts as are deposited in the Fund under section 3212; and
any interest earned on investment of amounts in the Fund under section 3214.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.content: For each of fiscal years 2017 through 2028, the Secretary of the Treasury shall deposit in the Fund $35,000,000 from the general fund of the Treasury.

subsection.heading: Availability of Amounts.—
subsection.content: Amounts deposited in the Fund under subsection (a) shall be used, subject to appropriation, to carry out this subtitle.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.chapeau: Subject to subsection (b), for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2028, the Secretary may, to the extent provided in advance in appropriations Acts, expend from the Fund, in accordance with this subtitle, not more than the sum of—

paragraph.content: the amount of interest accrued in the Fund.

subsection.heading: Additional expenditures.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may expend more than $35,000,000 for any fiscal year referred to in subsection (a) if the additional amounts are available in the Fund as a result of a failure of the Secretary to expend all of the amounts available under subsection (a) in 1 or more prior fiscal years.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of the Treasury shall invest such portion of the Fund as is not, in the judgment of the Secretary, required to meet current withdrawals.

subsection.heading: Credits to fund.—
subsection.content: The interest on, and the proceeds from the sale or redemption of, any obligations held in the Fund shall be credited to, and form a part of, the Fund.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.content: The amounts required to be transferred to the Fund under this part shall be transferred at least monthly from the general fund of the Treasury to the Fund on the basis of estimates made by the Secretary of the Treasury.

subsection.heading: Adjustments.—
subsection.content: Proper adjustment shall be made in amounts subsequently transferred to the extent prior estimates are in excess of or less than the amounts required to be transferred.

section.heading: TERMINATION.
section.chapeau: On September 30, 2028—

paragraph.content: the Fund shall terminate; and
the unexpended and unobligated balance of the Fund shall be transferred to the general fund of the Treasury.

part.heading: REPAIR, REPLACEMENT, AND MAINTENANCE OF CERTAIN INDIAN IRRIGATION PROJECTS

section.heading: REPAIR, REPLACEMENT, AND MAINTENANCE OF CERTAIN INDIAN IRRIGATION PROJECTS.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish a program to address the deferred maintenance needs and water storage needs of Indian irrigation projects that—

paragraph.content: create risks to public or employee safety or natural or cultural resources; and
unduly impede the management and efficiency of the Indian irrigation program.

subsection.heading: Funding.—
subsection.chapeau: Consistent with section 3213, the Secretary shall use or transfer to the Bureau of Indian Affairs not less than $35,000,000 of amounts in the Fund, plus accrued interest, for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2028 to carry out maintenance, repair, and replacement activities for 1 or more of the Indian irrigation projects described in section 3222 (including any structures, facilities, equipment, personnel, or vehicles used in connection with the operation of those projects), subject to the condition that the funds expended under this part shall not be—

paragraph.content: subject to reimbursement by the owners of the land served by the Indian irrigation projects; or
assessed as debts or liens against the land served by the Indian irrigation projects.

section.heading: ELIGIBLE PROJECTS.
section.chapeau: The projects eligible for funding under section 3221(b) are the Indian irrigation projects in the western United States that, on the date of enactment of this Act—

paragraph.content: are owned by the Federal Government, as listed in the Federal inventory required by Executive Order 13327 (40 U.S.C. 121 note; relating to Federal real property asset management);

are managed and operated by the Bureau of Indian Affairs (including projects managed, operated, or maintained under contracts or compacts pursuant to the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5301 et seq.); and
have deferred maintenance documented by the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

section.heading: REQUIREMENTS AND CONDITIONS.
section.chapeau: Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act and as a precondition to amounts being expended from the Fund to carry out this part, the Secretary, in consultation with the Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs and representatives of affected Indian tribes, shall develop and submit to Congress—

paragraph.chapeau: programmatic goals to carry out this part that—

subparagraph.content: would enable the completion of repairing, replacing, modernizing, or performing maintenance on projects as expeditiously as practicable;
facilitate or improve the ability of the Bureau of Indian Affairs to carry out the mission of the Bureau of Indian Affairs in operating a project;
ensure that the results of government-to-government consultation required under section 3225 be addressed; and
would facilitate the construction of new water storage using non-Federal contributions to address tribal, regional, and watershed-level supply needs; and

paragraph.chapeau: funding prioritization criteria to serve as a methodology for distributing funds under this part, that take into account—

subparagraph.content: the extent to which deferred maintenance of qualifying irrigation projects poses a threat to public or employee safety or health;
the extent to which deferred maintenance poses a threat to natural or cultural resources;
the extent to which deferred maintenance poses a threat to the ability of the Bureau of Indian Affairs to carry out the mission of the Bureau of Indian Affairs in operating the project;

subparagraph.chapeau: the extent to which repairing, replacing, modernizing, or performing maintenance on a facility or structure will—

clause.content: improve public or employee safety, health, or accessibility;
assist in compliance with codes, standards, laws, or other requirements;
address unmet needs; and
assist in protecting natural or cultural resources;

subparagraph.content: the methodology of the rehabilitation priority index of the Secretary, as in effect on the date of enactment of this Act;
the potential economic benefits of the expenditures on job creation and general economic development in the affected tribal communities;
the ability of the qualifying project to address tribal, regional, and watershed level water supply needs; and

such other factors as the Secretary determines to be appropriate to prioritize the use of available funds that are, to the fullest extent practicable, consistent with tribal and user recommendations received pursuant to the consultation and input process under section 3225.

section.heading: STUDY OF INDIAN IRRIGATION PROGRAM AND PROJECT MANAGEMENT.

subsection.heading: Tribal consultation and user input.—
subsection.chapeau: Before beginning to conduct the study required under subsection (b), the Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: consult with the Indian tribes that have jurisdiction over the land on which an irrigation project eligible to receive funding under section 3222 is located; and

paragraph.chapeau: solicit and consider the input, comments, and recommendations of—

subparagraph.content: the landowners served by the irrigation project; and
irrigators from adjacent irrigation districts.

subsection.heading: Study.—
subsection.content: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, acting through the Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs, shall complete a study that evaluates options for improving programmatic and project management and performance of irrigation projects managed and operated in whole or in part by the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: On completion of the study under subsection (b), the Secretary, acting through the Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs, shall submit to the Committee on Indian Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives a report that—

paragraph.content: describes the results of the study;
determines the cost to financially sustain each project;
recommends whether management of each project could be improved by transferring management responsibilities to other Federal agencies or water user groups; and

paragraph.chapeau: includes recommendations for improving programmatic and project management and performance—

subparagraph.content: in each qualifying project area; and
for the program as a whole.

subsection.heading: Status Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, and not less frequently than every 2 years thereafter (until the end of fiscal year 2028), the Secretary, acting through the Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs, shall submit to the Committee on Indian Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives a report that includes a description of—

paragraph.content: the progress made toward addressing the deferred maintenance needs of the Indian irrigation projects described in section 3222, including a list of projects funded during the fiscal period covered by the report;
the outstanding needs of those projects that have been provided funding to address the deferred maintenance needs pursuant to this part;
the remaining needs of any of those projects;

paragraph.chapeau: how the goals established pursuant to section 3223 have been met, including—

subparagraph.content: an identification and assessment of any deficiencies or shortfalls in meeting those goals; and
a plan to address the deficiencies or shortfalls in meeting those goals; and

paragraph.content: any other subject matters the Secretary, to the maximum extent practicable consistent with tribal and user recommendations received pursuant to the consultation and input process under section 3225, determines to be appropriate.

section.heading: TRIBAL CONSULTATION AND USER INPUT.
section.chapeau: Before expending funds on an Indian irrigation project pursuant to section 3221 and not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: consult with the Indian tribe that has jurisdiction over the land on which an irrigation project eligible to receive funding under section 3222 is located; and

paragraph.chapeau: solicit and consider the input, comments, and recommendations of—

subparagraph.content: the landowners served by the irrigation project; and
irrigators from adjacent irrigation districts.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.content: Subject to subsection (b), to the maximum extent practicable, the Secretary shall ensure that, for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2028, each Indian irrigation project eligible for funding under section 3222 that has critical maintenance needs receives part of the funding under section 3221 to address critical maintenance needs.

subsection.heading: Priority.—
subsection.content: In allocating amounts under section 3221(b), in addition to considering the funding priorities described in section 3223, the Secretary shall give priority to eligible Indian irrigation projects serving more than 1 Indian tribe within an Indian reservation and to projects for which funding has not been made available during the 10-year period ending on the day before the date of enactment of America’s Water Infrastructure Act of 2018 under any other Act of Congress that expressly identifies the Indian irrigation project or the Indian reservation of the project to address the deferred maintenance, repair, or replacement needs of the Indian irrigation project.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Subject to paragraph (2), in allocating amounts under section 3221(b), the Secretary shall allocate not more than $15,000,000 to any individual Indian irrigation project described in section 3222 during any consecutive 3-year period.

paragraph.heading: Exception.—
paragraph.content: Notwithstanding the cap described in paragraph (1), if the full amount under section 3221(b) cannot be fully allocated to eligible Indian irrigation projects because the costs of the remaining activities authorized in section 3221(b) of an irrigation project would exceed the cap described in paragraph (1), the Secretary may allocate the remaining funds to eligible Indian irrigation projects in accordance with this part.

subsection.heading: Basis of funding.—
subsection.content: Any amounts made available under this section shall be nonreimbursable.

subsection.heading: Applicability of ISDEAA.—
subsection.content: The Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5301 et seq.) shall apply to activities carried out under this section.

section.heading: PREPAYMENT OF CERTAIN REPAYMENT OBLIGATIONS UNDER CONTRACTS BETWEEN THE UNITED STATES AND THE WEBER BASIN WATER CONSERVANCY DISTRICT.
section.chapeau: The Secretary of the Interior shall allow for prepayment of repayment obligations under Repayment Contract No. 14-06-400-33 between the United States and the Weber Basin Water Conservancy District, dated December 12, 1952, and supplemented and amended on June 30, 1961, on April 15, 1966, on September 20, 1968, and on May 9, 1985, including future amendments and all related applicable contracts thereto, providing for repayment of Weber Basin Project construction costs allocated to irrigation and municipal and industrial purposes for which repayment is provided pursuant to such contracts under terms and conditions similar to those used in implementing the prepayment provisions in section 210 of the Central Utah Project Completion Act (Public Law 102-575), as amended, for prepayment of Central Utah Project, Bonneville Unit repayment obligations. The prepayment—

paragraph.content: shall result in the United States recovering the net present value of all repayment streams that would have been payable to the United States if this Act was not in effect;
may be provided in several installments;
may not be adjusted on the basis of the type of prepayment financing used by the District; and
shall be made such that total repayment is made not later than September 30, 2026.

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This subtitle may be cited as the “Pechanga Band of Luiseño Mission Indians Water Rights Settlement Act”.

section.heading: PURPOSES.
section.chapeau: The purposes of this subtitle are—

paragraph.chapeau: to achieve a fair, equitable, and final settlement of claims to water rights and certain claims for injuries to water rights in the Santa Margarita River Watershed for—

subparagraph.content: the Band; and
the United States, acting in its capacity as trustee for the Band and Allottees;

paragraph.content: to achieve a fair, equitable, and final settlement of certain claims by the Band and Allottees against the United States;
to authorize, ratify, and confirm the Pechanga Settlement Agreement to be entered into by the Band, RCWD, and the United States;

paragraph.chapeau: to authorize and direct the Secretary—

subparagraph.content: to execute the Pechanga Settlement Agreement; and
to take any other action necessary to carry out the Pechanga Settlement Agreement in accordance with this subtitle; and

paragraph.content: to authorize the appropriation of amounts necessary for the implementation of the Pechanga Settlement Agreement and this subtitle.

section.heading: DEFINITIONS.
section.chapeau: In this subtitle:

paragraph.heading: Adjudication court.—
paragraph.content: The term “Adjudication Court” means the United States District Court for the Southern District of California, which exercises continuing jurisdiction over the Adjudication Proceeding.

paragraph.heading: Adjudication proceeding.—
paragraph.content: The term “Adjudication Proceeding” means litigation initiated by the United States regarding relative water rights in the Santa Margarita River Watershed in United States v. Fallbrook Public Utility District et al., Civ. No. 3:51-cv-01247 (S.D.C.A.), including any litigation initiated to interpret or enforce the relative water rights in the Santa Margarita River Watershed pursuant to the continuing jurisdiction of the Adjudication Court over the Fallbrook Decree.

paragraph.heading: Allottee.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “Allottee” means an individual who holds a beneficial real property interest in an Indian allotment that is—

subparagraph.content: located within the Reservation; and
held in trust by the United States.

paragraph.heading: Band.—
paragraph.content: The term “Band” means Pechanga Band of Luiseño Mission Indians, a federally recognized sovereign Indian tribe that functions as a custom and tradition Indian tribe, acting on behalf of itself and its members, but not acting on behalf of members in their capacities as Allottees.

paragraph.heading: Claims.—
paragraph.content: The term “claims” means rights, claims, demands, actions, compensation, or causes of action, whether known or unknown.

paragraph.heading: EMWD.—
paragraph.content: The term “EMWD” means Eastern Municipal Water District, a municipal water district organized and existing in accordance with the Municipal Water District Law of 1911, Division 20 of the Water Code of the State of California, as amended.

paragraph.heading: EMWD connection fee.—
paragraph.content: The term “EMWD Connection Fee” has the meaning set forth in the Extension of Service Area Agreement.

paragraph.heading: Enforceability Date.—
paragraph.content: The term “enforceability date” means the date on which the Secretary publishes in the Federal Register the statement of findings described in section 3407(e).

paragraph.heading: ESAA capacity agreement.—
paragraph.content: The term “ESAA Capacity Agreement” means the “ESAA Capacity Agreement”, among the Band, RCWD, and the United States.

paragraph.heading: ESAA water.—
paragraph.content: The term “ESAA Water” means imported potable water that the Band receives from EMWD and MWD pursuant to the Extension of Service Area Agreement and delivered by RCWD pursuant to the ESAA Water Delivery Agreement.

paragraph.heading: ESAA water delivery agreement.—
paragraph.content: The term “ESAA Water Delivery Agreement” means the agreement among EMWD, RCWD, and the Band, establishing the terms and conditions of water service to the Band.

paragraph.heading: Extension of service area agreement.—
paragraph.content: The term “Extension of Service Area Agreement” means the “Extension of Service Area Agreement”, among the Band, EMWD, and MWD, for the provision of water service by EMWD to a designated portion of the Reservation using water supplied by MWD.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The term “Fallbrook Decree” means the “Modified Final Judgment And Decree”, entered in the Adjudication Proceeding on April 6, 1966.

subparagraph.heading: Inclusions.—
subparagraph.content: The term “Fallbrook Decree” includes all court orders, interlocutory judgments, and decisions supplemental to the “Modified Final Judgment And Decree”, including Interlocutory Judgment No. 30, Interlocutory Judgment No. 35, and Interlocutory Judgment No. 41.

paragraph.heading: Fund.—
paragraph.content: The term “Fund” means the Pechanga Settlement Fund established by section 3409.

paragraph.heading: Indian tribe.—
paragraph.content: The term “Indian tribe” has the meaning given the term in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5304).

paragraph.heading: Injury to water rights.—
paragraph.content: The term “injury to water rights” means an interference with, diminution of, or deprivation of water rights under Federal or State law.

paragraph.heading: Interim capacity.—
paragraph.content: The term “Interim Capacity” has the meaning set forth in the ESAA Capacity Agreement.

paragraph.heading: Interim capacity notice.—
paragraph.content: The term “Interim Capacity Notice” has the meaning set forth in the ESAA Capacity Agreement.

paragraph.heading: Interlocutory judgment no. 41.—
paragraph.content: The term “Interlocutory Judgment No. 41” means Interlocutory Judgment No. 41 issued in the Adjudication Proceeding on November 8, 1962, including all court orders, judgments, and decisions supplemental to that interlocutory judgment.

paragraph.heading: MWD.—
paragraph.content: The term “MWD” means the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, a metropolitan water district organized and incorporated under the Metropolitan Water District Act of the State of California (Stats. 1969, Chapter 209, as amended).

paragraph.heading: MWD connection fee.—
paragraph.content: The term “MWD Connection Fee” has the meaning set forth in the Extension of Service Area Agreement.

paragraph.heading: Pechanga esaa delivery capacity account.—
paragraph.content: The term “Pechanga ESAA Delivery Capacity account” means the account established by section 3409(c)(2).

paragraph.heading: Pechanga recycled water infrastructure account.—
paragraph.content: The term “Pechanga Recycled Water Infrastructure account” means the account established by section 3409(c)(1).

paragraph.heading: Pechanga settlement agreement.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “Pechanga Settlement Agreement” means the Pechanga Settlement Agreement, dated April 8, 2016, together with the exhibits to that agreement, entered into by the Band, the United States on behalf of the Band, its members and Allottees, MWD, EMWD, and RCWD, including—

subparagraph.content: the Extension of Service Area Agreement;
the ESAA Capacity Agreement; and
the ESAA Water Delivery Agreement.

paragraph.heading: Pechanga Water Code.—
paragraph.content: The term “Pechanga Water Code” means a water code to be adopted by the Band in accordance with section 3405(f).

paragraph.heading: Pechanga water fund account.—
paragraph.content: The term “Pechanga Water Fund account” means the account established by section 3409(c)(3).

paragraph.heading: Pechanga water quality account.—
paragraph.content: The term “Pechanga Water Quality account” means the account established by section 3409(c)(4).

paragraph.heading: Permanent capacity.—
paragraph.content: The term “Permanent Capacity” has the meaning set forth in the ESAA Capacity Agreement.

paragraph.heading: Permanent capacity notice.—
paragraph.content: The term “Permanent Capacity Notice” has the meaning set forth in the ESAA Capacity Agreement.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The term “RCWD” means the Rancho California Water District organized pursuant to section 34000 et seq. of the California Water Code.

subparagraph.heading: Inclusions.—
subparagraph.content: The term “RCWD” includes all real property owners for whom RCWD acts as an agent pursuant to an agency agreement.

paragraph.heading: Recycled water infrastructure agreement.—
paragraph.content: The term “Recycled Water Infrastructure Agreement” means the “Recycled Water Infrastructure Agreement” among the Band, RCWD, and the United States.

paragraph.heading: Recycled water transfer agreement.—
paragraph.content: The term “Recycled Water Transfer Agreement” means the “Recycled Water Transfer Agreement” between the Band and RCWD.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The term “Reservation” means the land depicted on the map attached to the Pechanga Settlement Agreement as Exhibit I.

subparagraph.heading: Applicability of term.—
subparagraph.content: The term “Reservation” shall be used solely for the purposes of the Pechanga Settlement Agreement, this subtitle, and any judgment or decree issued by the Adjudication Court approving the Pechanga Settlement Agreement.

paragraph.heading: Santa margarita river watershed.—
paragraph.content: The term “Santa Margarita River Watershed” means the watershed that is the subject of the Adjudication Proceeding and the Fallbrook Decree.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means the State of California.

paragraph.heading: Storage pond.—
paragraph.content: The term “Storage Pond” has the meaning set forth in the Recycled Water Infrastructure Agreement.

paragraph.heading: Tribal water right.—
paragraph.content: The term “Tribal Water Right” means the water rights ratified, confirmed, and declared to be valid for the benefit of the Band and Allottees, as set forth and described in section 3405.

section.heading: APPROVAL OF THE PECHANGA SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Except as modified by this subtitle, and to the extent that the Pechanga Settlement Agreement does not conflict with this subtitle, the Pechanga Settlement Agreement is authorized, ratified, and confirmed.

paragraph.heading: Amendments.—
paragraph.content: Any amendment to the Pechanga Settlement Agreement is authorized, ratified, and confirmed, to the extent that the amendment is executed to make the Pechanga Settlement Agreement consistent with this subtitle.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: To the extent that the Pechanga Settlement Agreement does not conflict with this subtitle, the Secretary is directed to and promptly shall execute—

subparagraph.content: the Pechanga Settlement Agreement (including any exhibit to the Pechanga Settlement Agreement requiring the signature of the Secretary); and
any amendment to the Pechanga Settlement Agreement necessary to make the Pechanga Settlement Agreement consistent with this subtitle.

paragraph.heading: Modifications.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this subtitle precludes the Secretary from approving modifications to exhibits to the Pechanga Settlement Agreement not inconsistent with this subtitle, to the extent those modifications do not otherwise require congressional approval pursuant to section 2116 of the Revised Statutes (25 U.S.C. 177) or other applicable Federal law.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: In implementing the Pechanga Settlement Agreement, the Secretary shall promptly comply with all applicable requirements of—

subparagraph.content: the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq.);
the Endangered Species Act of 1973 (16 U.S.C. 1531 et seq.);
all other applicable Federal environmental laws; and
all regulations promulgated under the laws described in subparagraphs (A) through (C).

paragraph.heading: Execution of the pechanga settlement agreement.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Execution of the Pechanga Settlement Agreement by the Secretary under this section shall not constitute a major Federal action under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq.).

subparagraph.heading: Compliance.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary is directed to carry out all Federal compliance necessary to implement the Pechanga Settlement Agreement.

paragraph.heading: Lead Agency.—
paragraph.content: The Bureau of Reclamation shall be designated as the lead agency with respect to environmental compliance.

subsection.heading: Intent of Congress.—
subsection.chapeau: It is the intent of Congress to provide to each Allottee benefits that are equal to or exceed the benefits Allottees possess as of the date of enactment of this Act, taking into consideration—

paragraph.content: the potential risks, cost, and time delay associated with litigation that would be resolved by the Pechanga Settlement Agreement and this subtitle;
the availability of funding under this subtitle;
the availability of water from the Tribal Water Right and other water sources as set forth in the Pechanga Settlement Agreement; and
the applicability of section 7 of the Act of February 8, 1887 (25 U.S.C. 381), and this subtitle to protect the interests of Allottees.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: A Tribal Water Right of up to 4,994 acre-feet of water per year that, under natural conditions, is physically available on the Reservation is confirmed in accordance with the Findings of Fact and Conclusions of Law set forth in Interlocutory Judgment No. 41, as affirmed by the Fallbrook Decree.

paragraph.heading: Use.—
paragraph.content: Subject to the terms of the Pechanga Settlement Agreement, this subtitle, the Fallbrook Decree, and applicable Federal law, the Band may use the Tribal Water Right for any purpose on the Reservation.

subsection.heading: Holding in Trust.—
subsection.chapeau: The Tribal Water Right, as set forth in subsection (b), shall—

paragraph.content: be held in trust by the United States on behalf of the Band and the Allottees in accordance with this section;
include the priority dates described in Interlocutory Judgment No. 41, as affirmed by the Fallbrook Decree; and
not be subject to forfeiture or abandonment.

paragraph.heading: Applicability of act of february 8, 1887.—
paragraph.content: The provisions of section 7 of the Act of February 8, 1887 (25 U.S.C. 381), relating to the use of water for irrigation purposes shall apply to the Tribal Water Right.

paragraph.heading: Entitlement to water.—
paragraph.content: Any entitlement to water of an Allottee under Federal law shall be satisfied from the Tribal Water Right.

paragraph.heading: Allocations.—
paragraph.content: Allotted land located within the exterior boundaries of the Reservation shall be entitled to a just and equitable allocation of water for irrigation and domestic purposes from the Tribal Water Right.

paragraph.heading: Exhaustion of remedies.—
paragraph.content: Before asserting any claim against the United States under section 7 of the Act of February 8, 1887 (25 U.S.C. 381), or any other applicable law, an Allottee shall exhaust remedies available under the Pechanga Water Code or other applicable tribal law.

paragraph.heading: Claims.—
paragraph.content: Following exhaustion of remedies available under the Pechanga Water Code or other applicable tribal law, an Allottee may seek relief under section 7 of the Act of February 8, 1887 (25 U.S.C. 381), or other applicable law.

paragraph.heading: Authority.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall have the authority to protect the rights of Allottees as specified in this section.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Except as provided in paragraph (2), the Band shall have authority to use, allocate, distribute, and lease the Tribal Water Right on the Reservation in accordance with—

subparagraph.content: the Pechanga Settlement Agreement; and
applicable Federal law.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: An Allottee may lease any interest in land held by the Allottee, together with any water right determined to be appurtenant to that interest in land.

subparagraph.heading: Water right appurtenant.—
subparagraph.content: Any water right determined to be appurtenant to an interest in land leased by an Allottee shall be used on such land on the Reservation.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 18 months after the enforceability date, the Band shall enact a Pechanga Water Code, that provides for—

subparagraph.content: the management, regulation, and governance of all uses of the Tribal Water Right in accordance with the Pechanga Settlement Agreement; and

establishment by the Band of conditions, permit requirements, and other limitations relating to the storage, recovery, and use of the Tribal Water Right in accordance with the Pechanga Settlement Agreement.

paragraph.heading: Inclusions.—
paragraph.chapeau: Subject to the approval of the Secretary, the Pechanga Water Code shall provide—

subparagraph.content: that allocations of water to Allottees shall be satisfied with water from the Tribal Water Right;
that charges for delivery of water for irrigation purposes for Allottees shall be assessed on a just and equitable basis;
a process by which an Allottee may request that the Band provide water for irrigation or domestic purposes in accordance with this subtitle;

subparagraph.chapeau: a due process system for the consideration and determination by the Band of any request by an Allottee (or any successor in interest to an Allottee) for an allocation of such water for irrigation or domestic purposes on allotted land, including a process for—

clause.content: appeal and adjudication of any denied or disputed distribution of water; and
resolution of any contested administrative decision; and

subparagraph.content: a requirement that any Allottee with a claim relating to the enforcement of rights of the Allottee under the Pechanga Water Code or relating to the amount of water allocated to land of the Allottee must first exhaust remedies available to the Allottee under tribal law and the Pechanga Water Code before initiating an action against the United States or petitioning the Secretary pursuant to subsection (d)(4).

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall administer the Tribal Water Right until the Pechanga Water Code is enacted and approved under this section.

subparagraph.heading: Approval.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Any provision of the Pechanga Water Code and any amendment to the Pechanga Water Code that affects the rights of Allottees—

clause.content: shall be subject to the approval of the Secretary; and
shall not be valid until approved by the Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: Approval period.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall approve or disapprove the Pechanga Water Code within a reasonable period of time after the date on which the Band submits the Pechanga Water Code to the Secretary for approval.

subsection.heading: Effect.—
subsection.chapeau: Except as otherwise specifically provided in this section, nothing in this subtitle—

paragraph.content: authorizes any action by an Allottee against any individual or entity, or against the Band, under Federal, State, tribal, or local law; or
alters or affects the status of any action pursuant to section 1491(a) of title 28, United States Code.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.content: The benefits provided to the Band under the Pechanga Settlement Agreement and this subtitle shall be in complete replacement of, complete substitution for, and full satisfaction of all claims of the Band against the United States that are waived and released pursuant to section 3407.

subsection.heading: Allottee Claims.—
subsection.chapeau: The benefits realized by the Allottees under this subtitle shall be in complete replacement of, complete substitution for, and full satisfaction of—

paragraph.content: all claims that are waived and released pursuant to section 3407; and
any claims of the Allottees against the United States that the Allottees have or could have asserted that are similar in nature to any claim described in section 3407.

subsection.heading: No Recognition of Water Rights.—
subsection.content: Except as provided in section 3405(d), nothing in this subtitle recognizes or establishes any right of a member of the Band or an Allottee to water within the Reservation.

subsection.heading: Claims Relating to Development of Water for Reservation.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The amounts authorized to be appropriated pursuant to section 3411 shall be used to satisfy any claim of the Allottees against the United States with respect to the development or protection of water resources for the Reservation.

paragraph.heading: Satisfaction of claims.—
paragraph.content: Upon the complete appropriation of amounts authorized pursuant to section 3411, any claim of the Allottees against the United States with respect to the development or protection of water resources for the Reservation shall be deemed to have been satisfied.

paragraph.heading: Waiver of claims by the band and the united states acting in its capacity as trustee for the band.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to the retention of rights set forth in subsection (c), in return for recognition of the Tribal Water Right and other benefits as set forth in the Pechanga Settlement Agreement and this subtitle, the Band, and the United States, acting as trustee for the Band, are authorized and directed to execute a waiver and release of all claims for water rights within the Santa Margarita River Watershed that the Band, or the United States acting as trustee for the Band, asserted or could have asserted in any proceeding, including the Adjudication Proceeding, except to the extent that such rights are recognized in the Pechanga Settlement Agreement and this subtitle.

subparagraph.heading: Claims against rcwd.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Subject to the retention of rights set forth in subsection (c) and notwithstanding any provisions to the contrary in the Pechanga Settlement Agreement, the Band and the United States, on behalf of the Band and Allottees, fully release, acquit, and discharge RCWD from—

clause.content: claims for injuries to water rights in the Santa Margarita River Watershed for land located within the Reservation arising or occurring at any time up to and including June 30, 2009;

claims for injuries to water rights in the Santa Margarita River Watershed for land located within the Reservation arising or occurring at any time after June 30, 2009, resulting from the diversion or use of water in a manner not in violation of the Pechanga Settlement Agreement or this subtitle;
claims for subsidence damage to land located within the Reservation arising or occurring at any time up to and including June 30, 2009;

claims for subsidence damage arising or occurring after June 30, 2009, to land located within the Reservation resulting from the diversion of underground water in a manner consistent with the Pechanga Settlement Agreement or this subtitle; and
claims arising out of, or relating in any manner to, the negotiation or execution of the Pechanga Settlement Agreement or the negotiation or execution of this subtitle.

paragraph.heading: Claims by the united states acting in its capacity as trustee for allottees.—
paragraph.content: Subject to the retention of claims set forth in subsection (c), in return for recognition of the Tribal Water Right and other benefits as set forth in the Pechanga Settlement Agreement and this subtitle, the United States, acting as trustee for Allottees, is authorized and directed to execute a waiver and release of all claims for water rights within the Santa Margarita River Watershed that the United States, acting as trustee for the Allottees, asserted or could have asserted in any proceeding, including the Adjudication Proceeding, except to the extent such rights are recognized in the Pechanga Settlement Agreement and this subtitle.

paragraph.heading: Claims by the band against the united states.—
paragraph.chapeau: Subject to the retention of rights set forth in subsection (c), the Band, is authorized to execute a waiver and release of—

subparagraph.content: all claims against the United States (including the agencies and employees of the United States) relating to claims for water rights in, or water of, the Santa Margarita River Watershed that the United States, acting in its capacity as trustee for the Band, asserted, or could have asserted, in any proceeding, including the Adjudication Proceeding, except to the extent that those rights are recognized in the Pechanga Settlement Agreement and this subtitle;

all claims against the United States (including the agencies and employees of the United States) relating to damages, losses, or injuries to water, water rights, land, or natural resources due to loss of water or water rights (including damages, losses or injuries to hunting, fishing, gathering, or cultural rights due to loss of water or water rights, claims relating to interference with, diversion, or taking of water or water rights, or claims relating to failure to protect, acquire, replace, or develop water, water rights, or water infrastructure) in the Santa Margarita River Watershed that first accrued at any time up to and including the enforceability date;

all claims against the United States (including the agencies and employees of the United States) relating to the pending litigation of claims relating to the water rights of the Band in the Adjudication Proceeding; and

all claims against the United States (including the agencies and employees of the United States) relating to the negotiation or execution of the Pechanga Settlement Agreement or the negotiation or execution of this subtitle.

subsection.heading: Effectiveness of Waivers and Releases.—
subsection.content: The waivers under subsection (a) shall take effect on the enforceability date.

subsection.heading: Reservation of Rights and Retention of Claims.—
subsection.chapeau: Notwithstanding the waivers and releases authorized in this subtitle, the Band, on behalf of itself and the members of the Band, and the United States, acting in its capacity as trustee for the Band and Allottees, retain—

paragraph.content: all claims for enforcement of the Pechanga Settlement Agreement and this subtitle;
all claims against any person or entity other than the United States and RCWD, including claims for monetary damages;
all claims for water rights that are outside the jurisdiction of the Adjudication Court;
all rights to use and protect water rights acquired on or after the enforceability date; and
all remedies, privileges, immunities, powers, and claims, including claims for water rights, not specifically waived and released pursuant to this subtitle and the Pechanga Settlement Agreement.

subsection.heading: Effect of Pechanga Settlement Agreement and Act.—
subsection.chapeau: Nothing in the Pechanga Settlement Agreement or this subtitle—

paragraph.chapeau: affects the ability of the United States, acting as a sovereign, to take actions authorized by law, including any laws relating to health, safety, or the environment, including—

subparagraph.content: the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (42 U.S.C. 9601 et seq.);
the Safe Drinking Water Act (42 U.S.C. 300f et seq.);
the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (33 U.S.C. 1251 et seq.); and
any regulations implementing the Acts described in subparagraphs (A) through (C);

paragraph.content: affects the ability of the United States to take actions acting as trustee for any other Indian tribe or an Allottee of any other Indian tribe;

paragraph.chapeau: confers jurisdiction on any State court—

subparagraph.content: to interpret Federal law regarding health, safety, or the environment;
to determine the duties of the United States or other parties pursuant to Federal law regarding health, safety, or the environment; or
to conduct judicial review of Federal agency action;

paragraph.content: waives any claim of a member of the Band in an individual capacity that does not derive from a right of the Band;

limits any funding that RCWD would otherwise be authorized to receive under any Federal law, including, the Reclamation Wastewater and Groundwater Study and Facilities Act (43 U.S.C. 390h et seq.) as that Act applies to permanent facilities for water recycling, demineralization, and desalination, and distribution of nonpotable water supplies in Southern Riverside County, California;

characterizes any amounts received by RCWD under the Pechanga Settlement Agreement or this subtitle as Federal for purposes of section 1649 of the Reclamation Wastewater and Groundwater Study and Facilities Act (43 U.S.C. 390h-32); or

affects the requirement of any party to the Pechanga Settlement Agreement or any of the exhibits to the Pechanga Settlement Agreement to comply with the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq.) or the California Environmental Quality Act (Cal. Pub. Res. Code 21000 et seq.) prior to performing the respective obligations of that party under the Pechanga Settlement Agreement or any of the exhibits to the Pechanga Settlement Agreement.

subsection.heading: Enforceability date.—
subsection.chapeau: The enforceability date shall be the date on which the Secretary publishes in the Federal Register a statement of findings that—

paragraph.content: the Adjudication Court has approved and entered a judgment and decree approving the Pechanga Settlement Agreement in substantially the same form as Appendix 2 to the Pechanga Settlement Agreement;
all amounts authorized by this subtitle have been deposited in the Fund;
the waivers and releases authorized in subsection (a) have been executed by the Band and the Secretary;

paragraph.chapeau: the Extension of Service Area Agreement—

subparagraph.content: has been approved and executed by all the parties to the Extension of Service Area Agreement; and
is effective and enforceable in accordance with the terms of the Extension of Service Area Agreement; and

paragraph.chapeau: the ESAA Water Delivery Agreement—

subparagraph.content: has been approved and executed by all the parties to the ESAA Water Delivery Agreement; and
is effective and enforceable in accordance with the terms of the ESAA Water Delivery Agreement.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each applicable period of limitation and time-based equitable defense relating to a claim described in this section shall be tolled for the period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act and ending on the earlier of—

subparagraph.content: April 30, 2030, or such alternate date after April 30, 2030, as is agreed to by the Band and the Secretary; or
the enforceability date.

paragraph.heading: Effects of subsection.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this subsection revives any claim or tolls any period of limitation or time-based equitable defense that expired before the date of enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Limitation.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this section precludes the tolling of any period of limitations or any time-based equitable defense under any other applicable law.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: If all of the amounts authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary pursuant to this subtitle have not been made available to the Secretary by April 30, 2030—

subparagraph.content: the waivers authorized by this section shall expire and have no force or effect; and
all statutes of limitations applicable to any claim otherwise waived under this section shall be tolled until April 30, 2030.

paragraph.heading: Voiding of Waivers.—
paragraph.chapeau: If a waiver authorized by this section is void under paragraph (1)—

subparagraph.content: the approval of the United States of the Pechanga Settlement Agreement under section 3404 shall be void and have no further force or effect;

any unexpended Federal amounts appropriated or made available to carry out this subtitle, together with any interest earned on those amounts, and any water rights or contracts to use water and title to other property acquired or constructed with Federal amounts appropriated or made available to carry out this subtitle shall be returned to the Federal Government, unless otherwise agreed to by the Band and the United States and approved by Congress; and

except for Federal amounts used to acquire or develop property that is returned to the Federal Government under subparagraph (B), the United States shall be entitled to set off any Federal amounts appropriated or made available to carry out this subtitle that were expended or withdrawn, together with any interest accrued, against any claims against the United States relating to water rights asserted by the Band or Allottees in any future settlement of the water rights of the Band or Allottees.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall, subject to the availability of appropriations, using amounts from the designated accounts of the Fund, provide the amounts necessary to fulfill the obligations of the Band under the Recycled Water Infrastructure Agreement and the ESAA Capacity Agreement, in an amount not to exceed the amounts deposited in the designated accounts for such purposes plus any interest accrued on such amounts from the date of deposit in the Fund to the date of disbursement from the Fund, in accordance with this subtitle and the terms and conditions of those agreements.

subsection.heading: Nonreimbursability of Costs.—
subsection.content: All costs incurred by the Secretary in carrying out this section shall be nonreimbursable.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall, using amounts from the Pechanga Recycled Water Infrastructure account, provide amounts for the Storage Pond in accordance with this section.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall, subject to the availability of appropriations, using amounts from the Pechanga Recycled Water Infrastructure account provide the amounts necessary for a Storage Pond in accordance with the Recycled Water Infrastructure Agreement, in an amount not to exceed $2,656,374.

subparagraph.heading: Procedure.—
subparagraph.content: The procedure for the Secretary to provide amounts pursuant to this section shall be as set forth in the Recycled Water Infrastructure Agreement.

subparagraph.heading: Liability.—
subparagraph.content: The United States shall have no responsibility or liability for the Storage Pond.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall, using amounts from the Pechanga ESAA Delivery Capacity account, provide amounts for Interim Capacity and Permanent Capacity in accordance with this section.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall, subject to the availability of appropriations, using amounts from the ESAA Delivery Capacity account, provide amounts necessary for the provision of Interim Capacity in accordance with the ESAA Capacity Agreement in an amount not to exceed $1,000,000.

subparagraph.heading: Procedure.—
subparagraph.content: The procedure for the Secretary to provide amounts pursuant to this section shall be as set forth in the ESAA Capacity Agreement.

subparagraph.heading: Liability.—
subparagraph.content: The United States shall have no responsibility or liability for the Interim Capacity to be provided by RCWD or by the Band.

subparagraph.heading: Transfer to band.—
subparagraph.content: If RCWD does not provide the Interim Capacity Notice required pursuant to the ESAA Capacity Agreement by the date that is 60 days after the date required under the ESAA Capacity Agreement, the amounts in the Pechanga ESAA Delivery Capacity account for purposes of the provision of Interim Capacity and Permanent Capacity, including any interest that has accrued on those amounts, shall be available for use by the Band to provide alternative interim capacity in a manner that is similar to the Interim Capacity and Permanent Capacity that the Band would have received had RCWD provided such Interim Capacity and Permanent Capacity.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall, subject to the availability of appropriations, using amounts from the ESAA Delivery Capacity account, provide amounts necessary for the provision of Permanent Capacity in accordance with the ESAA Capacity Agreement.

subparagraph.heading: Procedure.—
subparagraph.content: The procedure for the Secretary to provide funds pursuant to this section shall be as set forth in the ESAA Capacity Agreement.

subparagraph.heading: Liability.—
subparagraph.content: The United States shall have no responsibility or liability for the Permanent Capacity to be provided by RCWD or by the Band.

subparagraph.heading: Transfer to band.—
subparagraph.content: If RCWD does not provide the Permanent Capacity Notice required pursuant to the ESAA Capacity Agreement by the date that is 5 years after the enforceability date, the amounts in the Pechanga ESAA Delivery Capacity account for purposes of the provision of Permanent Capacity, including any interest that has accrued on those amounts, shall be available for use by the Band to provide alternative Permanent Capacity in a manner that is similar to the Permanent Capacity that the Band would have received had RCWD provided such Permanent Capacity.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: There is established in the Treasury of the United States a fund to be known as the “Pechanga Settlement Fund”, to be managed, invested, and distributed by the Secretary and to be available until expended, and, together with any interest earned on those amounts, to be used solely for the purpose of carrying out this subtitle.

subsection.heading: Transfers to Fund.—
subsection.content: The Fund shall consist of such amounts as are deposited in the Fund under section 3411(a) of this subtitle, together with any interest earned on those amounts, which shall be available in accordance with subsection (e).

subsection.heading: Accounts of Pechanga Settlement Fund.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish in the Fund the following accounts:

paragraph.content: Pechanga Recycled Water Infrastructure account, consisting of amounts authorized pursuant to section 3411(a)(1).
Pechanga ESAA Delivery Capacity account, consisting of amounts authorized pursuant to section 3411(a)(2).
Pechanga Water Fund account, consisting of amounts authorized pursuant to section 3411(a)(3).
Pechanga Water Quality account, consisting of amounts authorized pursuant to section 3411(a)(4).

subsection.heading: Management of Fund.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall manage, invest, and distribute all amounts in the Fund in a manner that is consistent with the investment authority of the Secretary under—

paragraph.content: the first section of the Act of June 24, 1938 (25 U.S.C. 162a);
the American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 4001 et seq.); and
this section.

subsection.heading: Availability of amounts.—
subsection.content: Amounts appropriated to, and deposited in, the Fund, including any investment earnings accrued from the date of deposit in the Fund through the date of disbursement from the Fund, shall be made available to the Band by the Secretary beginning on the enforceability date.

subsection.heading: Withdrawals by Band Pursuant to the American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Band may withdraw all or part of the amounts in the Fund on approval by the Secretary of a tribal management plan submitted by the Band in accordance with the American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 4001 et seq.).

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: In addition to the requirements under the American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 4001 et seq.), the tribal management plan under paragraph (1) shall require that the Band shall spend all amounts withdrawn from the Fund in accordance with this subtitle.

subparagraph.heading: Enforcement.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may carry out such judicial or administrative actions as the Secretary determines to be necessary to enforce the tribal management plan to ensure that amounts withdrawn by the Band from the Fund under this subsection are used in accordance with this subtitle.

subsection.heading: Withdrawals by Band Pursuant to an Expenditure Plan.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Band may submit an expenditure plan for approval by the Secretary requesting that all or part of the amounts in the Fund be disbursed in accordance with the plan.

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.content: The expenditure plan under paragraph (1) shall include a description of the manner and purpose for which the amounts proposed to be disbursed from the Fund will be used, in accordance with subsection (h).

paragraph.heading: Approval.—
paragraph.content: If the Secretary determines that an expenditure plan submitted under this subsection is consistent with the purposes of this subtitle, the Secretary shall approve the plan.

paragraph.heading: Enforcement.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may carry out such judicial or administrative actions as the Secretary determines necessary to enforce an expenditure plan to ensure that amounts disbursed under this subsection are used in accordance with this subtitle.

subsection.heading: Uses.—
subsection.chapeau: Amounts from the Fund shall be used by the Band for the following purposes:

paragraph.heading: Pechanga recycled water infrastructure account.—
paragraph.content: The Pechanga Recycled Water Infrastructure account shall be used for expenditures by the Band in accordance with section 3408(c).

paragraph.heading: Pechanga esaa delivery capacity account.—
paragraph.content: The Pechanga ESAA Delivery Capacity account shall be used for expenditures by the Band in accordance with section 3408(d).

paragraph.heading: Pechanga water fund account.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Pechanga Water Fund account shall be used for—

subparagraph.content: payment of the EMWD Connection Fee;
payment of the MWD Connection Fee; and
any expenses, charges, or fees incurred by the Band in connection with the delivery or use of water pursuant to the Pechanga Settlement Agreement.

paragraph.heading: Pechanga water quality account.—
paragraph.content: The Pechanga Water Quality account shall be used by the Band to fund groundwater desalination activities within the Wolf Valley Basin.

subsection.heading: Liability.—
subsection.content: The Secretary and the Secretary of the Treasury shall not be liable for the expenditure of, or the investment of any amounts withdrawn from, the Fund by the Band under subsection (f) or (g).

subsection.heading: No Per Capita Distributions.—
subsection.content: No portion of the Fund shall be distributed on a per capita basis to any member of the Band.

subsection.heading: Waiver of Sovereign Immunity by the United States.—
subsection.content: Except as provided in subsections (a) through (c) of section 208 of the Department of Justice Appropriation Act, 1953 (43 U.S.C. 666), nothing in this subtitle waives the sovereign immunity of the United States.

subsection.heading: Other Tribes Not Adversely Affected.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this subtitle quantifies or diminishes any land or water right, or any claim or entitlement to land or water, of an Indian tribe, band, or community other than the Band.

subsection.heading: Limitation on Claims for Reimbursement.—
subsection.chapeau: With respect to Indian land within the Reservation—

paragraph.content: the United States shall not submit against any Indian-owned land located within the Reservation any claim for reimbursement of the cost to the United States of carrying out this subtitle and the Pechanga Settlement Agreement; and
no assessment of any Indian-owned land located within the Reservation shall be made regarding that cost.

subsection.heading: Effect on Current Law.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section affects any provision of law (including regulations) in effect on the day before the date of enactment of this Act with respect to preenforcement review of any Federal environmental enforcement action.

paragraph.heading: Pechanga recycled water infrastructure account.—
paragraph.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $2,656,374, for deposit in the Pechanga Recycled Water Infrastructure account, to carry out the activities described in section 3408(c).

paragraph.heading: Pechanga esaa delivery capacity account.—
paragraph.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $17,900,000, for deposit in the Pechanga ESAA Delivery Capacity account, which amount shall be adjusted for changes in construction costs since June 30, 2009, as is indicated by ENR Construction Cost Index, 20-City Average, as applicable to the types of construction required for the Band to provide the infrastructure necessary for the Band to provide the Interim Capacity and Permanent Capacity in the event that RCWD elects not to provide the Interim Capacity or Permanent Capacity as set forth in the ESAA Capacity Agreement and contemplated in sections 3408(d)(2)(D) and 3408(d)(3)(D) of this subtitle, with such adjustment ending on the date on which funds authorized to be appropriated under this section have been deposited in the Fund.

paragraph.heading: Pechanga water fund account.—
paragraph.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $5,483,653, for deposit in the Pechanga Water Fund account, which amount shall be adjusted for changes in appropriate cost indices since June 30, 2009, with such adjustment ending on the date of deposit in the Fund, for the purposes set forth in section 3409(h)(3).

paragraph.heading: Pechanga water quality account.—
paragraph.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $2,460,000, for deposit in the Pechanga Water Quality account, which amount shall be adjusted for changes in appropriate cost indices since June 30, 2009, with such adjustment ending on the date of deposit in the Fund, for the purposes set forth in section 3409(h)(4).

section.heading: EXPIRATION ON FAILURE OF ENFORCEABILITY DATE.
section.chapeau: If the Secretary does not publish a statement of findings under section 3407(e) by April 30, 2021, or such alternative later date as is agreed to by the Band and the Secretary, as applicable—

paragraph.content: this subtitle expires on the later of May 1, 2021, or the day after the alternative date agreed to by the Band and the Secretary;
any action taken by the Secretary and any contract or agreement pursuant to the authority provided under any provision of this subtitle shall be void;
